label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=4)
explanation: Fires almost only on the delimiter step (99.9% of activation mass), and only when the sequence is short. Rate at <DEL> is about 92% for L=3, about 51% for L=4, about 12% for L=5 and essentially zero for L>=6. Shorter sequences give larger activations: L=3 makes up 30% of mass on far fewer steps. Within L=4 the token content modulates firing in a diffuse way. It is more likely when the first token is i, j, l, v, c or 3 and less likely when there are many digits, and the top examples begin with l, g or 3. No simple token rule captured this (adding a first-token set raises precision to 0.85 but halves recall). It does not fire during the original-input phase and essentially never during the copy phase (67 copy steps, scattered). Dev: P 0.64, R 0.84, F1 0.73, mass recall 0.92.
